tier_reason: Well-known independent third-party suite (krausest/js-framework-benchmark, Chrome 154 results committed 2026-10-04) whose raw run arrays in webdriver-ts-results/src/results.ts contain both yew-v0.23.0-keyed and react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed; benchmark code (webdriver-ts) and Yew's release profile (frameworks/keyed/yew/Cargo.toml) are public, but no CPU model or machine is stated for this snapshot (releases.json gives no note for Chrome 148-154), so B not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'Achieves high performance by minimizing DOM API calls for each page render' (no number). Suite data for the yew-v0.23.0-keyed entry (struct components, impl Component): unweighted geometric mean over the 9 CPU benchmarks of the median total duration is 0.819x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed (about 1.22x faster, derived from page data); swap 1,000 rows 13.8 ms vs React 89.7 ms; create 1,000 rows 31.7 ms vs React 23.6 ms; create 10,000 rows 325.6 ms vs React 401.0 ms; versus react-classes-v19.0.0-keyed 0.822x; versus vanillajs-keyed 1.492x (slower). Excluding swap rows the geometric mean is 1.009x React hooks' time (no win), and Yew's own hooks implementation (yew-hooks-v0.23.0-keyed) is 1.030x React hooks' time, i.e. not faster (all derived from page data).
corrections.workload: krausest/js-framework-benchmark (Chrome 154 snapshot): nine WebDriver-driven Chrome benchmarks on a 1,000/10,000-row table (create, replace all, partial update, select, swap, remove, create 10k, append, clear; partial update, select, swap and clear run with 4x CPU throttling, remove with 2x), median of 15 runs (25 for select) of the total (script plus paint) duration. Yew entry is yew-v0.23.0-keyed (frameworks/keyed/yew, struct components); a separate yew-hooks-v0.23.0-keyed entry uses function components with hooks.
corrections.hardware: Not stated for the Chrome 154 snapshot (results commit 2026-10-04); webdriver-ts-results/releases.json labels Chrome 139-146 'macOS' but gives no note for Chrome 148-154 and no CPU model anywhere.
corrections.caveats: Independent public suite but the CPU model for this snapshot is not stated, so tier B not A. The whole geometric-mean win over React comes from swap rows (React hooks 89.7 ms vs 13.8 ms, a known React reconciliation weakness): excluding swap, Yew's struct-component entry is 1.009x React hooks' time. Yew is slower than React on create 1,000 rows (1.34x of React's time), replace all rows (1.18x) and append rows (1.22x). The like-for-like hooks implementation (yew-hooks-v0.23.0-keyed, function components) is 1.030x React hooks' time, so idiomatic modern Yew is not faster; the struct-component entry is 0.822x React classes. Not faster than vanilla JS (1.492x its time) or the best JS frameworks: geometric-mean slowdown versus the per-benchmark best over all keyed and non-keyed entries is 1.21 vanillajs-keyed, 1.34 Solid, 1.44 Svelte, 1.81 Yew (1.56 for Yew against keyed-only best); all derived from page data, unweighted, not the site's weighted geometric mean. Among keyed Rust/Wasm entries Yew ranks behind wasm-bindgen, spair, silkenweb, stdweb, dominator, leptos, dioxus, mogwai and sycamore; only yew-hooks and sauron are slower. Wasm implementations are checked in as prebuilt bundles ('build-prod is a no-op, the generated javascript is already provided'), so the shipped binary may not match current source. The implementation carries benchmark note #1139 (does not pass strict CSP), which does not affect timings. Category fit is weak: Yew is a Rust/Wasm UI framework, not a wasm-targeting language.

notes: All quoted numbers match the yew-v0.23.0-keyed row of results.ts (medians re-derived: 0.819x vs React hooks, 1.492x vs vanilla). Main shortcomings: win rests entirely on swap rows (1.009x React's time without it), Yew's hooks variant is 1.030x React hooks (not faster), slower than vanilla JS and most Rust frameworks; the record's 'slowest Rust framework' caveat was wrong (sauron and yew-hooks are slower) and is corrected. Metadata checked on github.com: Apache-2.0 and MIT, 32.8k stars, last commit 2026-08-26, not archived; category would fit wasm-libraries-and-apps better than assemblyscript-and-wasm-langs.
